prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1231; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the claimant regarding a sideswipe that occurred while changing lanes. The claimant reports a shoulder injury and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene. Both the police and the reporting parties confirm this detail.

Entry 4: Photos taken at the scene confirm some key details of the collision. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the photos are the main independent record of the event.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle damage, which is consistent with the impact described by the claimant. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection notes.

Entry 6: Spoke with the claimant again today. The account of the lane change and impact matches what was given in the first notice and in each prior conversation.

Entry 7: Reviewed the medical file. The reported shoulder injury fits the kind and force of this crash. Treatment followed a typical course and tapered off as the claimant improved. Records note a minor strain in the same area several years ago that healed fully.

Entry 8: Based on the damage, the medical course, and the consistent statements, the claim is progressing normally. Next step is to finalize the injury evaluation and issue the settlement offer.
